identificationModule.briefTitle: Predicting Response to Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 Immunotherapy by Plasma Extracellular Vesicle Analysis
identificationModule.officialTitle: Predicting Response to Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 Immunotherapy by Plasma Extracellular Vesicle Analysis

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
The objective of this prospective multicenter study is to evaluate whether the analysis of immunological biomarkers present in circulating extracellular vesicles is associated with the response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 treatments in patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or unresectable melanoma.

Patients will receive standard-of-care treatment and will be followed according to routine clinical practice. The study involves the collection of four study-specific blood samples at different time points during follow-up, as well as the collection of standard immunohistochemistry results, thoraco-abdomino-pelvic CT scans, and tumor DNA genotyping analyses performed as part of routine care.

The study aims to determine:

* whether baseline biomarkers in extracellular vesicles are associated with response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 treatment,
* how these biomarkers change over the course of treatment, and
* to provide exploratory data for the development of predictive immunological response signatures.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) have become standard treatment for patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or melanoma. However, not all patients respond to these therapies, and current biomarkers are imperfect.

Circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanovesicles derived from tumor and immune cells, carrying proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids. They represent an accessible and stable source of immunological biomarkers, allowing monitoring of the tumor microenvironment without additional invasive procedures.

This prospective multicenter study aims to determine, in a prospective cohort of patients with locally advanced or metastatic lung cancer or melanoma, the impact of baseline immune biomarkers present in extracellular vesicles on response to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy

Secondary objectives have also been defined :

* To evaluate the association between longitudinal changes in EV-associated immune biomarkers during follow-up and response to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.
* To develop a predictive score (immune signature) of response to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy by combining baseline EV-associated immune biomarkers.
* To stratify analyses by tumor type (NSCLC versus melanoma) to determine whether tumor-specific characteristics influence the predictive performance of the identified immune signature.
* To obtain preliminary evidence on the contribution of EV-associated biomarkers to the prediction of primary or secondary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.
* In the NSCLC cohort, to compare the predictive performance of the EV-based score with that of a score based solely on the tumor expression (assessed on biopsy specimens) of immunosuppressive proteins, without incorporating EV-associated biomarkers, for predicting best overall response (BOR) at 6 months.
* To explore EV-derived miRNA profiles in responders and non-responders.
* In each cohort, to compare the predictive performance of the EV-based score with that of a score integrating tumor mutational biomarkers derived from ctDNA and/or tumor tissue DNA for predicting BOR at 6 months.
* To evaluate PFS, including PFS at 6 and 12 months, as well as median PFS.
* To establish a prospective plasma biobank from patients treated with anti-PD-(L)1 therapies for future retrospective analyses following completion of the EVpredict study in the field of cancer immunology

Study procedures for participants include:

* Blood sample collection: Four study-specific blood draws performed during standard treatment or tumor assessment visits (baseline, 2nd administration, first evaluation, second evaluation).
* Collection of additional information: Standard immunohistochemistry results thoraco-abdomino-pelvic CT scans; circulating or tumor DNA genotyping analyses.
* Clinical follow-up: Conducted according to routine care standards, with no changes to treatment or additional study-specific visits.

armGroups.label: Advanced NSCLC or Melanoma - Anti-PD-(L)1 Therapy
armGroups.description:
This cohort includes patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or inoperable melanoma who are receiving standard-of-care anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, either as monotherapy or in combination with other approved therapies.

Participants will follow standard clinical management, and study-specific procedures include four blood draws for extracellular vesicle (EV) analysis at baseline and during follow-up, collection of standard immunohistochemistry results (PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4, Tim-3, LAG-3, TIGIT), thoraco-abdominopelvic CT imaging, and tumor DNA genotyping performed as part of routine care.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Target protein levels in plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) measured by multiplex ELISA before treatment
primaryOutcomes.description: Treatment response assessed as Best Overall Response (BOR: complete or partial response per RECIST 1.1) within 6 months.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Association of EV-Associated Target Protein Concentrations With Best Overall Response at 6 Months
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Development of a Predictive Score Based on Baseline EV-Associated Biomarkers for Best Overall Response at 6 Months
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Predictive Performance of the EV-Based Score for Best Overall Response
secondaryOutcomes.description: Predictive performance will be assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and, following score dichotomization, sensitivity and specificity. Performance for predicting BOR will be evaluated in the overall cohort and separately in the NSCLC and melanoma cohorts.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: EV-Associated Target Protein Concentrations in Non-Responders to Anti-PD-(L)1 Therapy
secondaryOutcomes.description: Analysis of target protein concentrations in EVs at baseline and during follow-up in non-responders according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. These preliminary data will provide an initial assessment of the feasibility of a future clinical trial evaluating the therapeutic benefit of EV analysis for guiding treatment decisions regarding immune checkpoint inhibitor combination therapies in patients with solid tumors.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Comparison of the Predictive Performance of Tumor Immunohistochemistry and the EV-Based Score in the NSCLC Cohort
secondaryOutcomes.description: In the NSCLC cohort, immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of target protein expression (including PD-L1) will be performed on diagnostic tumor biopsy specimens. The predictive performance of this approach will be compared with that of the EV-based score using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses and the AUC.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Comparison of EV-Derived miRNA Expression Profiles Between Responders and Non-Responders
secondaryOutcomes.description: EV-derived miRNA expression profiles at baseline and during follow-up will be analyzed by RT-qPCR and compared between responders and non-responders.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Comparison of the Predictive Performance of Tumor DNA Biomarkers and the EV-Based Score
secondaryOutcomes.description: Analysis of tumor DNA, including ctDNA and/or tumor tissue DNA, will be performed by next-generation sequencing (NGS) at diagnosis and at disease progression. The predictive performance of these biomarkers will be compared with that of the EV-based score using ROC curve analyses and the corresponding AUC.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At diagnosis and at disease progression; BOR assessed at 6 months after treatment initiation

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) at 6 and 12 Months and Median PFS
secondaryOutcomes.description: PFS will be defined as the time from study inclusion to disease progression, as assessed according to RECIST 1.1 criteria, or death from any cause, whichever occurs first. Patients who are alive without documented progression will be censored at the date of their last known follow-up. Median PFS, as well as PFS rates at 6 and 12 months, will be described
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the date of enrollment in the study until the first occurrence of disease progression or death, or up to 12 months after enrollment

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Storage of Residual Plasma Samples for Future Retrospective Analyses
secondaryOutcomes.description: Residual plasma samples remaining after completion of the study-specific analyses will be stored for future retrospective analyses in participants who have provided consent for biological sample collection. Additional and more in-depth analyses of biomarkers of interest may be performed based on the results generated during the EVpredict study.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 15 years after the end of the study

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* Histologically confirmed diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or locally advanced/metastatic unresectable melanoma.
* Patient scheduled to initiate anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, either as monotherapy or in combination (other immune checkpoint inhibitors, chemotherapy, etc.).
* Baseline tumor assessment performed within 28 days prior to enrollment (CT scan of thorax, abdomen, and pelvis) with at least one measurable lesion according to RECIST 1.1 criteria.
* Life expectancy \>6 months.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-2 at enrollment.
* Patient able to provide informed consent and comply with study procedures.
* Patient covered by a social security system or equivalent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior treatment with immunotherapy.
* Presence of EGFR or ALK mutation (applicable only to the lung cohort).
* Presence of another synchronous malignancy.
* Diagnosis of uveal melanoma.
* Treatment with systemic immunosuppressants, including within 28 days prior to enrollment, or corticosteroids \>10 mg/day, including within 14 days prior to enrollment.
* Disease not measurable according to RECIST 1.1 criteria.
* Positive serology for HIV, HBV, or HCV.
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
* Inability to comply with study follow-up and visits for geographic, social, or psychological reasons.
* Individuals deprived of liberty or under legal guardianship (including curatorship).
eligibilityModule.studyPopulation: Patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or melanoma, locally advanced or metastatic, and unresectable. For all patients, first-line standard treatment will be based on standard care with an anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, either as monotherapy or in combination (with other immune checkpoint inhibitors or chemotherapy). Standard treatments are defined by the approved indications (marketing authorizations) in France.
